parsed.explanation: The counterexample is valid: excluding the empty and full subsets leaves only 2^{n+1}-2 sums in (0,1), which yields at best a gap below 1/(2^{n+1}-3), not d. No other passage proves the required universal close-subset-sum claim. Replace this paragraph by ordering all 2^{n+1} subset sums, including 0 and 1; their 2^{n+1}-1 consecutive gaps sum to 1, so one gap is at most d. The remaining cancellation and construction then apply.
